newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money rates up on repo announcement.
newsitem.headline: India call money rates up on repo announcement.

text.p: Indian call money was trading higher at 4.00-4.50 percent on Monday compared to the previous close of 3.50-3.75 percent, dealers said.
"Call opened at 4.50 percent and is expected to remain at the same level for the rest of the fortnight," a dealer at Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India said.
"Repo auction will see a cut-off to 4.50 percent and it will attract more bidders due to the easy money condition prevailing in the market," he said.
The repo auction will prevent the call rates from sliding down from current low levels of 4.50 percent, he said.

"If the cut-off is 6.0 percent, the amount mopped up would be 6000 million rupees, while if it 5.0 percent it would mop up 4000 million rupees and if it is 4.5 percent, it would be in the range of 2500 to 3000 million rupess," Vinod Dixit, manager at Centurion Bank in Bombay said.
